original_question: Must every smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type be rigid?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right target almost verbatim: the paper's §1.3 asks whether every smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type is rigid. The quantifier, the hypotheses "smooth," "Q-acyclic," and "of log-general type," and the conclusion "rigid" all match the paper's intended statement.
missing_details: The paper's ambient setting is that of complex algebraic surfaces; to make the question stand-alone, the surface should be specified as a smooth complex algebraic surface (and, in context, an open/affine one).
"Q-acyclic" should be unpacked as having the rational homology of a point, e.g. H_i(X; Q)=0 for all i>0 (equivalently H_0(X; Q)≅Q and higher rational homology vanishes).
"Log-general type" should be made explicit as meaning logarithmic Kodaira dimension kappa(X)=2; §1.1 is where the paper states that kappa denotes the logarithmic Kodaira dimension.
The note itself does not define "rigid" inside §1.3; for a fully stand-alone version one should indicate that this is rigidity in the deformation-theoretic sense (no nontrivial deformations).

Your draft does not indicate that the neighboring numerical statement §1.4, involving a minimal SNC-completion (V,D) and the condition K_V(K_V+D)=0, is only an induced conjecture in the paper, not the primary statement you are targeting.
refined_question: Conjecture (Flenner–Zaidenberg). Let X be a smooth complex affine algebraic surface with the rational homology of a point, i.e. H_0(X; Q) ≅ Q and H_i(X; Q)=0 for all i>0. If X is of log-general type, equivalently if its logarithmic Kodaira dimension satisfies kappa(X)=2, must X be rigid (in the deformation-theoretic sense, i.e. admit no nontrivial deformations)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's §1.3 exactly: "Any smooth Q-acyclic surface X of log-general type is rigid." This is the nearest official formulation and should not be replaced by the nearby numerical Conjecture 1.4, because §1.4 is presented only as a conjecture induced by the Rigidity Conjecture, not as an equivalent restatement. The surrounding context in §1.1 supplies that kappa denotes logarithmic Kodaira dimension and that the section concerns smooth complex algebraic surfaces. To make the question stand-alone, the implicit meanings of Q-acyclic and log-general type should be spelled out, and the standard deformation-theoretic meaning of rigid should be made explicit even though the note itself leaves that term undeveloped.
